newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bank UBK 1996 net slumps.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bank UBK 1996 net slumps.

text.p: Slovenian bank UBK said on Thursday its preliminary net profit slumped to 11.7 million tolars ($74.300) from 120 million in 1995.

"The profit was down because of a large fall in corporate deposits at our bank following the bankruptcy of Komercialna banka Triglav (KBT) in July last year," Vlasta Grjol, UBK's executive director of global finances, told Reuters.

She said the bankruptcy of KBT, which had a domestic market share of about 1.8 percent and was closed after it ran into liquidity problems, caused widespread mistrust of smaller Slovenian banks amid domestic customers.
UBK, whose market stake is below 0.9 percent, said its balance sheet assets decreased to 13.2 billion tolars from 16.5 billion in June 1996 and from 13.9 billion at the end of 1995.
Grjol said the bank had not yet decided whether it would pay a dividend this year and added the decision would be taken at the next shareholders' meeting, presumably in June.
"If we decide to pay a dividend it could be unchanged from last year because of the reserves we kept from the 1995 profit," Grjol said.
Last year's dividend for UBK's shares B, which are listed on the main market of the Ljubljana bourse, was 720 tolars per share.
The bank earlier on Thursday said it was mulling a merger with another domestic bank, and that the link-up could happen as early as the second half of the current year.

Some 28 banks operate in Slovenia's tiny financial market, and analysts say a wave of mergers is inevitable as cost cutting pressures mount and banks have to prepare for the onset of foreign competition in line with European Union regulations. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
